text:
alex: quick proposal — we should decide between two approaches for capacity-based fallback when the primary model is saturated: prefetch-compatible spill (try compatible variants ahead of time) vs on-call fallback (route at the moment of saturation). thoughts?

maria: +1 we need to be clear about signal sources. prefetch reduces p99 spikes but increases avg cost if mispredicted.

jamal: what's the plan for tenant priority? if high-tier tenant gets prefetched slots that could starve low-tier requests.

alex: good call. thinking: precedence = tenant_tier -> region_affinity -> compatibility_score. Prefetch only grabs minimal warm slots, marked with tenant_owner so it doesn't evict others.

liz: UX question: on the Console, how do we show these prefetch reservations? right now the model pool view is already dense. need a subtle indicator. :thinking_face:   

ops-bot: [notice] autoscaler adjusted pool `redwood-gpu-pool-5` by +2 GPUs due to 10m sustained queue.

maria: console idea: a toggle per-rollout "prefetch fallback" with an expected cost delta and a probe success metric. show probe hit rate for last 30m.

jamal: telemetry: we need distinct metrics so we can attribute cost to prefetch vs actual routed tokens. propose: `fallback.prefetch.tokens`, `fallback.oncall.tokens`, `fallback.prefetch.mispredictions`.

sam: agree. also need latency buckets: prefetch should preserve p50/p95 but if mispredicted you might waste long-tail GPU cycles.

alex: API change suggestion — add `fallback_policy` to the route config: `{"mode":"off|oncall|prefetch","budget_pct":int, "eviction_signal":"tenant|least_recent"}`. example: 

```
route_config := {
  "model": "gptx-6b",
  "fallback_policy": {"mode":"prefetch","budget_pct":10,"eviction_signal":"least_recent"}
}
```
maria: prefer explicit `budget_pct` instead of slot count so it scales with pool size. but need hard cap guardrails.

jamal: eviction_signal names: `tenant` (evict lower-tier tenants first), `least_recent` (LRU), `cost` (evict by expected token cost). add `sticky_session` behavior: once a request is routed to variant X, subsequent requests within TTL should prefer X to avoid jitter.

liz: on Console: show a small badge on the route page: "Fallback: prefetch (10% budget)" + link to breakdown. users should be able to toggle `sticky_session_ttl` slider.

sam: ops question — what about cross-region prefetch? If primary saturates in us-west, should we prefetch in eu-west? that's network cost tradeoff.

alex: initially block cross-region prefetch to keep latency predictable. allow only oncall cross-region as a fallback if regional capacity exhausted and latency SLO allows.

maria: rollout plan: start with `mode=oncall` default for all routes, enable `prefetch` as opt-in for select customers. run A/B comparing p99 latency and token cost over 2 weeks.

jamal: telemetry to track: `fallback.predicted_hit_rate`, `fallback.actual_hit_rate`, `eviction.count`, `eviction.by_signal`, `route.sticky_hits`. Need these in the Console trend charts.

ops-bot: [alert] route `acct:enterprise-42 / gptx-6b` saw 15% overflow to fallback in last 1h.

sam: small API note: adding `fallback_policy` should be versioned on the route schema. don't break older SDK clients.

alex: agree; we'll add as optional v2 field. fallback decisions remain server-side; clients don't need to change.

maria: one more safety: if prefetch misprediction rate > 30% for 10m, auto-disable prefetch for that route and emit a notice with sample prompts for debugging.

jamal: and add a dry-run mode for prefetch where we simulate reservations and report simulated metrics before billing. helps customers approve the cost.

liz: Console UI: show dry-run toggle and a little explainer tooltip. Also surface "sample prompts" that hit the fallback so SEs can add triggers.

alex: ops implementation detail: prefetch reservations should be marked `eviction_exempt=false` but carry `owner_route_id`. eviction logic must prefer evictable=True && owner_tier_lower. ensure we don't evict reserved slots for existing active requests.

sam: can we incorporate tenant quotas? i.e., budget_pct per-route but also global per-tenant cap. need to avoid runaway costs.

maria: yes — layering: route_budget_pct -> tenant_max_pct -> org_max_pct. Console will show effective budget after layering.

jamal: question about metrics tagging: tag fallback metrics with `tenant_id`, `route_id`, `region`, `variant`. essential for drilldowns.

alex: sounds good. I'll draft the API PR and a small RFC for eviction prioritization. volunteers to review?

liz: I can do Console mocks. will post screenshots in the thread tomorrow. :slightly_smiling_face:

sam: I'll take telemetry schema and dashboards.

maria: I'll sketch rollout gating and the automatic disable logic.

jamal: I'll write the eviction heuristics and a few unit tests for the allocator.

alex: perfect — thanks. tagging follow-ups: @liz @sam @maria @jamal — please add ETA comments in the PR.

ops-bot: [note] thread pinned to #eng-platform for 48h.

liz: posted initial mock: https://redwood.internal/console-mock/prefetch-ui (screenshot + annotations).

sam: telemetry schema PR: https://git.redwood/telemetry/fallback-metrics (WIP).

maria: RFC draft: https://git.redwood/design/fallback-prefetch (WIP) — includes cost/benefit simulation.

jamal: allocator PR opened: https://git.redwood/infra/allocator/prefetch-eviction (WIP). includes LRU + tenant-priority modes.

alex: awesome. we'll sync next Tue in infra sync. thanks everyone. :rocket:
